title: Micron expanded multi-year Strategic Customer Agreements and supply commitments
canonical_summary: Micron's multi-year Strategic Customer Agreements used take-or-pay, quantity and price-band terms, customer commitments and reserved capacity to increase forward demand and pricing visibility while leaving delivery and cash-conversion questions open.
known_event_summary: August 31-September 8, 2026 Micron strategic-customer-contract update: sixteen agreements and roughly $22 billion of commitments or deposits, price floors/bands and reserved 2027 capacity were described alongside a broader long-term-contract order book.

facts.proposition: Customers have locked in $22 billion in supply commitments with Micron.
Micron completed 16 Strategic Customer Agreements (SCAs).
Micron states that its Strategic Customer Agreements generally use take-or-pay commitments with fixed pricing or pricing bands.
Take-or-pay supply contracts secure high margins for Micron while capping upside potential.
CEO Sanjay Mehrotra stated that multi-year Strategic Customer Agreements will significantly enhance the durability and predictability of Micron's strong financial performance.
A significant portion of Micron's 2027 production capacity is reserved through long-term customer agreements.
Micron Technology is unable to fulfill its entire order book.
Micron claims that contract minimum prices should generate gross margins well above previous peak quarterly margins.
A significant portion of Micron's 2027 capacity has been reserved.
Micron expects $22 billion of customer deposits and related financial commitments.
Micron's new strategic customer agreements require customers to commit to specific purchase volumes.
Most of Micron's strategic customer contracts have fixed prices or set minimum and maximum prices.
Micron and its rivals have begun locking in long-term contracts for up to five years.
Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra stated that strategic customer agreements will significantly enhance the durability and predictability of the company's strong financial performance.
Micron has $22 billion in commitments serving as collateral.
The composition of Micron's long-term contracts regarding DRAM/NAND versus HBM weighting is uncertain.
Sixteen strategic customer agreements carry $22 billion in commitments.
Micron holds $100B in long-term contracts.
Ceilings on existing products in Micron's new agreements could limit shortage-driven upside across contracted volumes.
Micron's new agreements provide valuable price floors.
